I have one. I've played it for twelve hours so far.

The console is small and the joycons are tiny. Too small to be comfortable for me. The pro controller is just about perfect though.

The UI is nice and clean and very fast. There's no bloat on it, and it's not trying to be a media centre or a PC in a box. It has games, and a shop to buy games, and some systems settings. Going from the game to the dash back to the game takes less than a second, it's pretty much instant. You can take screenshots and post them to Facebook or Twitter. They got rid of Miiverse (which I actually liked) but I can understand why; moderating that place was a time and money sink. You can also store them on a removable micro SD card if you want to transfer them. The posting tools also allow you to apply text and basic filters and things, perfect for meme-bait I suppose.

The unit is solidly built and feels good in the hand. It doesn't feel cheap and it's not too light or too heavy. The screen is really nice, great viewing angles, nice colours, bit of a dust magnet though.

Zelda is amazing. I'm having an absolute blast with it. There are so many little touches that, even for a frame-rate nazi like myself, I'm willing to overlook dips (that are apparently some kind of bug that only happens in docked mode?) because I'm just having fun.

Whether it will work as a primary console, especially in (((CURRENT YEAR + 2))) where a console is expected to also do every fucking thing else but play games it seems, remains to be seen, but BOTW at least proves Nintendo had at least one more GOTY up their sleeve.

At the very least, I can see the Switch being the secondary console of choice, it's just up to Nintendo not to drop the ball on a solid and consistent lineup of games. If they can do that, then I'd say in a year (perhaps even by Christmas when there's a 3D Mario, Mario Kart, Splatoon, Tetris, pretty much every genre covered with some big-name title) then it will be hard to pass up.

Having said that, apart from a handful of a launch titles and a few titles next month, the first year drought that consoles are known for is in full effect. Unless you're content to play one or two big games and a handful of indie eshop titles, you're probably better off waiting for a bigger library.

It looks like another gimmicky toy and I'm willing to bet its a piece of shit like everything else Nintendo has done in recent times, Ex; under powered hardware and rehashing the same games over and over
